0.headline: Milky Mist Share Price Live: Milky Mist's D-Street debut shortly; should you buy, sell or hold?
0.heading: Milky Mist Share Price Live: Milky Mist's D-Street debut shortly; should you buy, sell or hold?
0.intro: The current Milky Mist Dairy Food IPO GMP of Rs 18 translates into a 13% premium over the upper price band of Rs 140. At this premium, the indicative listing price works out to around Rs 158 per share.
0.body:
Milky Mist Dairy Food IPO shares are set to make their Dalal Street debut at 10 am today, August 18, after the finalisation of the share allotment. Ahead of the listing, the grey market is signalling a positive start for the dairy company, with its shares commanding a premium of Rs 18.

The current Milky Mist Dairy Food IPO GMP of Rs 18 translates into a 13% premium over the upper price band of Rs 140. At this premium, the indicative listing price works out to around Rs 158 per share.

However, the grey market premium has moderated sharply in the past three days, falling from Rs 29 to Rs 18. Market observers attributed the decline partly to the tepid mood in the broader secondary market.

Even so, observers said the current GMP represents the minimum return being indicated by the grey market. A reversal in market sentiment could provide further support to the IPO and potentially push the listing gain towards 20%.

In a bullish scenario, a 20% premium over the IPO's upper price band could translate into a listing price of around Rs 169 per share. This means the grey market is currently pointing to a potential listing gain of around 13%, with the upside potentially extending towards 20% if market sentiment improves.

However, stock market experts cautioned that GMP should not be treated as a reliable indicator of the actual listing premium, as it is not linked to the company's balance sheet or fundamentals. Investors should therefore base their view on the company's financial performance and fundamentals rather than relying solely on grey market trends.

1.headline: Shankesh Jewellers IPO to open on August 18; anchor investors acquire over Rs 110 crore worth shares
1.heading: Shankesh Jewellers IPO to open on August 18; anchor investors acquire over Rs 110 crore worth shares
1.intro: Shankesh Jewellers IPO | The company has tapped the capital markets with the aim of raising Rs 367.18 crore through its maiden public issue of 3.94 crore equity shares.
1.body:
Mumbai-based handcrafted gold jewellery distributor Shankesh Jewellers has mobilised Rs 110.15 crore through its anchor book on August 17. The fundraising took place ahead of the IPO opening for public subscription from August 18 to August 20.

The company has tapped the capital markets with the aim of raising Rs 367.18 crore through its maiden public issue of 3.94 crore equity shares, comprising a fresh issuance of 2.94 crore shares worth Rs 274.18 crore, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) of 1 crore shares amounting to Rs 93 crore.

The price band for the offer has been fixed at Rs 88-93 per share, valuing the company at Rs 1,367.4 crore.

Shankesh Jewellers, which undertakes outsourcing of handcrafted gold jewellery for several clients, including Joyalukkas India, P N Gadgil &amp; Sons, Kalyan Jewellers India, Manoj Vaibhav Gems ‘N’ Jewellers, Novel Jewels (Aditya Birla Group), Bhima Jewellery Madurai, Hari D P Abhushan, and Gajaananda Jewellery Mart India, has allocated 1.18 crore equity shares to 14 anchor investors.

Tiger Strategies Fund was the biggest buyer among the anchor investors, acquiring 18.4 lakh shares worth Rs 17.13 crore, followed by Necta Bloom One, which picked up 16.12 lakh shares amounting to Rs 15 crore. Venus Investment, Zeal Global Opportunities Fund, and ASAS Global Fund each bought 10.75 lakh shares worth Rs 10 crore.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Uni Growth Fund, Sunrise Investment Trust, Innovative Vision Trust, Nexus Global Opportunities Fund, Arnesta Global Opportunities Fund, Nova Global Opportunities Fund, Compact Structure Fund, 31 Degrees North Growth Fund, and Viney Growth Fund were the other investors that participated in the company's anchor book.

Kantilal Kheemraj Jain-promoted Shankesh Jewellers intends to utilise Rs 158 crore of the proceeds from the net fresh issue to repay debt, out of total outstanding borrowings of Rs 162.9 crore as of June 2026.

Further, Rs 38 crore will be utilised for its working capital requirements, while the remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes.

On the financial front, the company reported a profit of Rs 106.7 crore for the fiscal year ended March 2026, soaring 164.6 percent from Rs 40.3 crore in the previous year. Revenue from operations rose 16.2 percent to Rs 1,630.8 crore from Rs 1,403.8 crore during the same period.

The merchant bankers managing the Shankesh Jewellers IPO are Aryaman Financial Services and Smart Horizon Capital Advisors.

2.headline: Film producer Vipul Shah's Sunshine Pictures raises Rs 85 crore via anchor book ahead of Rs 282-crore IPO
2.heading: Film producer Vipul Shah's Sunshine Pictures raises Rs 85 crore via anchor book ahead of Rs 282-crore IPO
2.intro: Sunshine Pictures IPO | The company is targeting to mobilise Rs 282.1 crore through its initial public offering of 78.37 lakh shares at the higher end of the price band of Rs 342-360 per share.
2.body:
Film producer Vipul Shah and his wife Shefali-promoted Sunshine Pictures has raised Rs 84.64 crore from nine anchor investors on August 17, a day before the IPO opens for public subscription.

The company is targeting to mobilise Rs 282.1 crore through its initial public offering (IPO) of 78.37 lakh shares at the higher end of the price band of Rs 342-360 per share. The IPO consists of a fresh issuance of 48 lakh shares worth Rs 172.8 crore, while both promoters will sell 30.37 lakh shares amounting to Rs 109.3 crore via offer-for-sale.

The issue will open for public subscription from August 18 to August 20, 2026.

Sunshine Pictures, the producer of films such as The Kerala Story, Commando: A One-Man Army, and Holiday: A Soldier Is Never Off Duty, has allocated 23.51 lakh shares to anchor investors at the upper end of the price band.

Uni Growth Fund emerged as the biggest buyer among the anchor investors, buying 5.55 lakh shares for nearly Rs 20 crore, followed by Khandelwal Finance, Zeal Global Opportunities Fund, The Asia Fund VCC, and Shine Star Build Cap, which each picked up 2.77 lakh shares amounting to Rs 10 crore.

Other investors that participated in the anchor book were Innovative Vision Fund, Arnesta Global Opportunities Fund, Visionary Value Fund, and LRSD Securities.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Mumbai-based Sunshine Pictures intends to utilise Rs 112.5 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue for its working capital requirements, while the remaining funds will be set aside for general corporate purposes. The proceeds from the offer for sale will be received by the promoters.

On the financial front, the company reported a standalone profit of Rs 40.02 crore and revenue of Rs 74.43 crore for the fiscal year ended March 2026.

GYR Capital Advisors is acting as the merchant banker for the Sunshine Pictures IPOSunshine Pictures IPO.
